featured.name: Old Phone Revival
featured.tagline: Give the drawer phone a job
featured.blurb: Turn a retired handset into a lab: vulnerable targets to attack, servers to host, and a honeypot that texts you when something bites. Nothing here needs root.

featured.name: Stock Phone
featured.tagline: No root, no unlock, no risk
featured.blurb: Everything that works on a completely untouched Android 10+ device. Around two thirds of the catalogue, and none of it voids anything.

featured.name: Termux Bootstrap
featured.blurb: Every CLI package in the catalogue. Termux packages are not APKs, so developer verification does not touch a single one of them.

featured.name: No-Root Privilege
featured.blurb: Pair over wireless debugging and get ADB-level control with no root, no PC, and no bootloader unlock. Debloat, AppOps, package control.

featured.name: Field Kit
featured.blurb: Evidence capture, notes, offline maps, comms and credentials. The unglamorous half that decides whether the report gets written.

featured.name: Mobile App Testing
featured.blurb: jadx, apktool, Frida, objection and an on-device intercepting proxy — plus the vulnerable apps to point them at.

featured.name: RF & Hardware
featured.blurb: SDR receivers, NFC and MIFARE tooling, BLE, LoRa, and the OTG serial console that talks to all of your bench hardware.

featured.name: Network Recon
featured.tagline: See the network you are on
featured.blurb: Capture, scan, map and intercept. Most of it works unprivileged; the raw-socket half is marked so you know before you need it.

featured.name: Egress Control
featured.blurb: Per-app firewall, WireGuard, Tor, and turning the phone into a proxy so a laptop can pivot through it.

featured.name: Full NetHunter
featured.blurb: Everything that needs a NetHunter kernel. Read the Tier 3 warnings before you flash anything — this is the tier that bricks phones.
